entities.name: Diary of Anne Frank
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
Diary of Anne Frank was a personal and poignant record of life in hiding during the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands. Created by Anne Frank in 1942, it details her daily experiences as a 13-year-old Jewish girl living with her family in secret to evade persecution. The diary chronicles their struggles, fears, and hopes for survival, offering a unique insight into the human cost of the Holocaust. Its significance extends beyond its personal context, influencing generations of readers and scholars alike. It has been translated into over 60 languages and remains one of the most widely read and studied diaries in history.

The diary's significance lies in its ability to convey the emotional and psychological toll of living under occupation, as well as its impact on the world stage. The Frank family's experiences are a testament to the resilience of human spirit in the face of unimaginable adversity. The diary has been the subject of numerous adaptations, interpretations, and scholarly analyses, cementing its place in the annals of modern history.

The diary's legacy extends beyond its literary significance, serving as a powerful educational tool for understanding the Holocaust and its consequences. It has also inspired countless works of art, literature, and music, ensuring its relevance to contemporary audiences.

One striking statistic is that over 10 million copies of the diary have been sold worldwide, making it one of the best-selling books of all time. A direct attributed quote from Anne Frank reads: 'In spite of everything, I still believe that people are truly good at heart.'

This enduring cultural footprint is a testament to the power of Anne Frank's story to transcend time and geography, speaking directly to hearts around the world.
